topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: Defocused reflector gain loss reduces peak gain, broadening beam patterns and increasing spillover loss, affecting link budget margins for SNR. This results in decreased capacity due to increased interference. Mitigation techniques like additional feed elements or curved arrays can compensate for gain loss.
reference_context: Defocused reflectors suffer 6 dB gain loss and beam broadening, impacting co-polar isolation and frequency reuse.
